extracted.intended_audience: tech/internet journalists, editors, and readers deciding what to cover (esp. AI, crypto, and platform/Internet reporting)
extracted.subtask_description: A compact editorial framework for deciding which tech/internet (especially AI and crypto) stories merit coverage and which should be deflated. Emphasizes empirical grounding, attention to adoption and material consequences, and skepticism toward hype-driven narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real product changes vs. marketing announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish actual product changes from marketing/PR announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor stories grounded in real, observable product changes (availability, features, deployments) and demote pieces that are primarily marketing spin or promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption data vs. founder claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer empirical adoption data over unverified claims made by founders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek measurable evidence that people or organizations are using a product/technology; be skeptical of narratives driven only by founders' or companies' assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material consequences vs. discourse-only events
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize stories with tangible material consequences rather than events that exist mainly in discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on developments that change behavior, economics, or systems rather than those confined to online chatter or punditry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bubble pattern recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag recurring hype cycles and patterns indicative of a bubble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for repetition of past hype dynamics; use historical pattern recognition to judge whether current enthusiasm reflects substantive change or cyclical overexcitement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and money flows
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze who benefits from a narrative — the flows of power and money behind a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogate incentives: identify actors profiting from attention, investment, or regulation, and make those beneficiaries explicit in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail vs. peak-hype timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider timing: whether a story is part of a long-term trend or a short-lived peak of hype; decide when to write the deflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer coverage that situates developments on a long-term axis (adoption/outcomes) rather than reacting to momentary peaks; time critical/contextual pieces to maximize insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is anyone actually using this? (adoption test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct test of adoption: determine whether the technology/product is actually in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this question as a quick filter to demand evidence of real-world usage before amplifying hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whose investment thesis is this story serving?
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask whose interests the story advances — which investment or reputational thesis benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this test to reveal conflicts of interest and whether coverage is being shaped to support particular financial or status-seeking agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the breathlessness warranted by the substance?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the excited tone of coverage matches the underlying substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that sensational or breathless reporting is supported by empirical facts, measurable impact, or clear mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year embarrassment test
rubrics_metrics.description: "What would a sophisticated reader 5 years from now find embarrassing about how this is being covered?" — a foresight-based skepticism check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use retrospective imagination to identify ephemeral angles or overclaims that are unlikely to age well; this helps avoid amplifying transient narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: AGI / 'everything will change' essays without empirical content
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprioritize sweeping AGI/transformative essays that lack empirical grounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating speculative grand claims as news unless they are supported by measurable evidence or demonstrable mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: Founder / VC narrative pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Downgrade stories that primarily replay founder or VC narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about amplifying origin stories or investor-friendly framings that don't provide independent verification or broader significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: Token / coin price stories without structural significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Deemphasize price-centric crypto coverage that lacks connection to structural or systemic significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only elevate token/coin price reporting when it reflects or implies substantive network, regulatory, or economic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: Influencer takes recycled
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid repeating high-volume influencer takes that add little original evidence or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat recycled influencer commentary as low-value unless it brings new data or materially different perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Adoption-rate measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize reporting that measures adoption rates and real-world uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that quantify who is using a technology and how fast adoption is progressing should be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Energy / labor / supply chain accountings
rubrics_metrics.description: Value accounts of energy, labor, and supply-chain impacts of new technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should include analyses of the resource and labor implications of deploying technologies, not just abstract promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Critical histories of similar past hypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Give prominence to histories that critically examine past hypes similar to current ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize new claims by comparing them to prior cycles, showing what repeated and what differed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Cultural reception / vernacular use
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize reporting on how people actually use and talk about new tools in everyday life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight vernacular adoption, cultural reception, and emergent use-cases that reveal real-world effects beyond marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Legal / regulatory inflections
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay attention to legal and regulatory developments and their practical implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on regulatory shifts and legal decisions that materially change incentives, constraints, or power dynamics around technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeptical-but-curious stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a stance that interrogates phenomena seriously without inflating them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be both curious about potential significance and skeptical of unsupported claims — take phenomena seriously enough to examine them, but avoid amplifying hype.
